A park ranger $P$ stands $900\,\text{ft}$ away from the base of a lookout tower $T$ to track a drone $D$ that is ascending vertically. The angle of elevation $\theta $ formed by the ranger and the drone is increasing at a rate of $\frac{\pi }{60}$ radians per second. At what rate is the drone gaining altitude at the moment when $\theta ={45}^{∘}?$ Do not round the answer.

The drone’s altitude is increasing at a rate of
{{field-1}}
$\text{ft/s}.$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14212968/assets/d30d2927efb6e85c408ba113499e043f72d726267e114e853690ac788c3946b1.png)

 

In the figure, $x$ is the distance between the ranger and the drone's takeoff position, and $y$ is the altitude of the drone. The quantity $x=900\,\text{ft}$ does not change with time because the distance between the ranger and the takeoff position is fixed.

We wish to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}.$ To do this, let's start by setting up a relation between $x$ and $y.$ Relative to the angle $\theta ,$ the sides $x$ and $y$ are the adjacent and opposite, respectively. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\frac{y}{x} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\frac{y}{900} \\ y & =900\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(900\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =900{sec}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given information, we have $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}=\frac{\pi }{60}$ and $\theta ={45}^{∘}.$ Substituting these values into the above, we reach

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =900{sec}^{2}⁡({45}^{∘})(\frac{\pi }{60}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =900{(\sqrt{2})}^{2}(\frac{\pi }{60}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =30\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the drone's altitude is increasing at a rate of $30\pi \,\text{ft/s}.$
